title: Anthropic Just Revealed How Their Engineers Use Claude Code
summary: Walks through Felix Rieseberg's essay on being more ambitious with models: ask for outcomes instead of tasks, and push on altitude, depth and range. Give the agent real resources and an outside judge so it can work toward the result rather than the next step.

title: Claude Mods Are Insane... You Need To Try These Right Now
summary: Anthropic's new Claude mods are always-on extensions that can redraw Claude Code's UI and change its behavior, unlike skills or plugins that only add capabilities. The channel builds mods for prompt enhancement, assumption tracking, session dashboards, same-folder session coordination, an idea shelf, and plain-language answer rewriting checked by a Haiku model. The idea worth keeping is the assumptions-review mod: surface every silent assumption the agent made, let a human mark each right or wrong, and automatically feed the wrong ones back as a correction prompt.

title: Google Just Fixed AI Design By Releasing This
summary: Google's Stitch design tool now ships a CLI, so Claude Code can drive it directly without the Google Cloud MCP setup, and it loads into context only when needed. The video builds a workflow of an interview-generated brief.md, Stitch designs, a build from them, then two review skills (design-fidelity and responsive screenshots, then a harsh 'story review' judged against the brief). The idea worth keeping is a written brief as the single source of truth, plus separate review-skill passes that catch what the generating agents miss.

title: GitHub's #1 Trending Skill Is Insane (5 Use Cases)
summary: The video shows 'Reverse Engineer Anything' (REA), an MCP server with ~170 tools that lets Claude Code trace browser behavior down to the exact network requests and code, saving each capture as evidence tagged seen/guessed/unknown. It demos five uses: cloning features from other apps, competitor research, black-box feature testing (caught a price-shown vs price-charged mismatch invisible in code), performance/layout audits, and security scans for leaked keys and access-control flaws. The idea worth keeping is the evidence-labelling discipline, where every agent finding must cite captured proof, and black-box QA of a running app with no code access as a review-loop step.

title: 6 Insane Trending GitHub AI Design Repos You Need to Use
summary: A roundup of six GitHub repos that give coding agents better design inputs: an Awards MCP for studying real award-winning sites, Responsively for multi-viewport screenshot checks, Genjutsu skills (including Bunshin, a sub-agent build-and-review loop), Dem Brand for extracting a site's styles into design.md, App Store Screenshots, and Brag for launch videos. The idea worth keeping is Bunshin's pattern: a lead agent sets a shared style, sub-agents build pages in parallel, and reviewer agents send problems back for fixes. The rounds stop at a round limit, when only minor issues remain, or when a round fixes nothing, though results varied by style.

title: Vercel's CEO Just Unveiled The Greatest AI Coding Workflow Ever
summary: Vercel's CEO describes working with AI agents: test ideas in throwaway projects, track whether the work is drifting from the plan rather than how much is shipped, and use adversarial agents to stress-test, scan for security debt and act on customer feedback fast. The video (AI Labs) turns this into seven tips, with commands and agents like a direction-drift checker, a breaker agent, and a first-time-user agent restricted by a hook to only running the app. The idea worth keeping is a drift check that compares what agents built against the PRD/spec folder, since building is cheap and agents never push back on scope.
